summary.text: Shomari Figures is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District, elected in 2024. A Mobile native and University of Alabama law graduate, he worked in the Obama White House and Department of Justice, for Sen. Sherrod Brown, and as deputy chief of staff and counselor to Attorney General Merrick Garland under President Biden. He sits on the House Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is seeking a second term.

paragraphs.text: Raised in Mobile, Alabama, and educated there from kindergarten through law school, according to his congressional biography; his father, Michael Figures, was a state senator and lawyer, and his mother, Vivian Figures, served on the Mobile City Council and is a state senator.
Graduated from John L. LeFlore High School in Mobile; earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and history (2006) and a J.D. (2010), both from the University of Alabama.
Clerked for a judge on the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri and worked on President Obama's re-election campaign.

In the Obama administration, served in the White House as Domestic Director of Presidential Personnel and then as White House Liaison at the Department of Justice, according to his congressional website.
Worked in the office of U.S. Senator Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio); his congressional website also lists service as Counsel in Congress.
Worked on the Biden-Harris transition team, then returned to the Department of Justice as deputy chief of staff and counselor to Attorney General Merrick Garland.
Won the April 16, 2024 Democratic primary runoff over Anthony Daniels (61.1%) and the November 2024 general election over Republican Caroleene Dobson (54.6% to 45.4%) in the redrawn 2nd District.
Assigned to the House Agriculture Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee for 2025-2026.
Advanced from the 2026 Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot; married to Dr. Kalisha Dessources Figures, with four children, according to his congressional website.
